newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says mechanical fault downed air force jet.
newsitem.headline: Manila says mechanical fault downed air force jet.

text.p: A mechanical fault apparently caused the crash of a Philippine Air Force F-5 fighter jet last week which killed its pilot and a man on the ground, the military said on Tuesday.

Armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera said the plane's elevator, a device at the tail that allows the plane to go up or down, got stuck while the pilot was taking off preventing him from controlling the plane.
"Investigators have found out that something went wrong with the elevator...Nothing definite about it but that seems to be the cause of the accident," he told reporters.
The plane crashed after it failed to gain altitude while performing a flypast during an official ceremony at an air base north of Manila.
The aircraft was one of three F-5s acquired by the Philippines from South Korea two years ago for a token amount of about $100, said a military spokesman who asked not to be identified.
Acedera has ordered the temporary grounding of the country's 10 other F-5s, mostly acquired from the United States in the 1960s, for checks and maintainance.
